name: Oversized hoodies

card.summary: Loose, boxy hooded sweatshirts from streetwear culture that people wear to change their silhouette and create a relaxed, layered look.

quick.overview:
An oversized hoodie is a hooded sweatshirt cut larger and boxier than a standard fit, with wide shoulders, a roomy body and often dropped sleeves. It is a staple of streetwear and is worn to create a relaxed silhouette.

The look comes from hip-hop and skate fashion of the 1980s and 1990s, and boxy hoodies in muted tones were pushed further into the mainstream by designers such as Kanye West in 2015. People wear them for comfort and for how the shape changes their outline.
quick.how: Wearers choose a size or cut larger than their normal fit, often pairing a boxy top with trousers that balance the volume, such as straight or tapered pants and sneakers. Heavyweight fabrics and neutral colours are a common choice in streetwear. Effects are immediate and depend on the outfit.
quick.risks: There are no health risks specific to the garment. Because the fit is loose, it hides the body's outline, which some wearers want and others find reduces the visibility of their physique.

lead: An oversized hoodie is a hooded pullover or zip-up deliberately worn or cut larger than the body, producing a loose, boxy silhouette. The hoodie began in the 1930s as workwear for laborers in cold New York warehouses, produced by Champion in Rochester, and gained its streetwear identity in the 1970s with hip-hop culture in New York City [1].

Baggy, oversized silhouettes are tied to the 1980s and 1990s streetwear scene: brands such as Stussy in California, and New York shops such as Union, which opened in 1989 to serve the baggy, oversized underground look, helped spread the style [2]. In 2015 Kanye West's Yeezy collection moved fashion toward muted, oversized tees and boxy hoodies without visible logos [2].

As a way to change how a body or outfit looks, an oversized hoodie works through proportion: a wide, structured top creates a broader, blockier outline on the upper body and a casual, layered impression.

chain: Upper-body outline becomes wider and more structured
Relaxed streetwear look that can be balanced with slimmer trousers
angle.text: Wearers use the garment to change their silhouette immediately. A boxy top adds visual width at the shoulders and torso and reads as deliberate streetwear styling.

paras: The hoodie's roots reach back to medieval hooded garments such as the cowl and chaperon, and the modern pullover began as laborers' workwear [1]. It became associated with hip-hop in the 1970s and with skaters and surfers in California in the 1990s, and designers including Tommy Hilfiger, Giorgio Armani and Ralph Lauren brought it into mainstream collections [1].

Streetwear grew from graffiti, hip-hop, skateboarding, surf and punk in the 1980s. Tokyo labels in the 1990s, including Nowhere, opened by Nigo and Jun Takahashi in 1993, refined New York's baggy silhouettes with better construction [2]. In 2018 Virgil Abloh became artistic director of menswear at Louis Vuitton, marking streetwear's entry into luxury fashion, and Supreme and Off-White made hoodies a luxury item [2].
Fashion retailers describe the boxy hoodie as distinct from simply large clothing, focusing on width and structure; those descriptions come from commercial sources and are not authoritative.

The hoodie has carried social meanings beyond fashion. In the UK it became linked in the 2000s with debates over anti-social behaviour, and in the US it became tied to discussions of race and crime after the 2012 shooting of Trayvon Martin and later became a protest symbol [1].

timeline.event: Champion produces the hooded pullover as workwear [1].
Hoodie adopted by hip-hop culture in New York City [1].
Union opens in New York for the baggy, oversized look [2].
Kanye West's Yeezy collection shows muted, oversized tees and boxy hoodies [2].
